look_here_first: Look for the gray cast before anything else: this is the short, low vervain whose stems and leaves are densely covered in stiff whitish hairs, giving the entire plant a canescent or dusty-gray appearance.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: low perennial, commonly under about 30 cm in the Williamson County treatment

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems and leaves densely hirsute/canescent, producing a gray-green appearance

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: opposite sessile to subsessile leaves, elliptic to oblong or nearly linear

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf margins with only a few teeth or short lobes rather than deep major divisions

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx and rachis conspicuously hairy, including pustulate-based hairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: four one-seeded mericarps with strongly pitted outer faces

key_traits.label: Verbena training
key_traits.text: Separate these by leaf architecture + hair texture + spike/branching architecture before using flower color.
